title: Partition String Into Minimum Beautiful Substrings
summary: Given a binary string, divide it into the fewest possible beautiful substrings.
statement: Given a binary string, divide it into the fewest possible beautiful substrings. A substring is beautiful if it lacks leading zeros and represents a power of five in binary. If division is impossible, return -1.
constraints: Partition the binary string into nonempty contiguous substrings.
Every part must have no leading zero and represent a positive power of five.
Return the minimum part count, or -1 if impossible.
hints: Precompute binary representations of powers of five.
Let dp[i] be the fewest valid parts covering the first i bits.
For every end, test all earlier starts whose substring is a power representation.
Every partition has a unique final cut, so minimizing over valid final parts exhausts all solutions.
editorial: Every partition has a unique final cut, so minimizing over valid final parts exhausts all solutions.

tests.explanation: Split as 101 and 1, representing five and one, so two parts suffice.
A leading-zero part is forbidden, so no partition exists.
